subject: Fee tilt and dealer routing for marketplace private offer
messages:
From: Maria Torres <maria@cloudops.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cloudops.com
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace private offer — pricing structure and channel routing question

Hi Rishi / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at CloudOps is excited about Redwood’s latency/price profile for generator workloads. Procurement asked me to get alignment on two things before we move to legal:

1) Private-offer pricing: we need a clear mapping of list price vs. committed tiers across AWS Marketplace. We currently have an internal rule that list price cannot vary by more than 12% region-to-region — can Redwood provide an example grid for a multi-region private offer?

2) Channel margin routing: we work with a distributor (NorthGate) and want to confirm how partner compensation flows on a private offer. Do you support a dealer margin pass-through vs. reseller netback? If you can outline the expected accounting path (who gets the SKU-level passback) that would help procurement.

Attached is our internal procurement checklist (see reference). Would you be able to send a draft private-offer PDF and a simple SKU-to-margin mapping? We’d like to get procurement and our distributor on a short call early next week.

Appreciate it —
Maria Torres
Head of Cloud Procurement
CloudOps Inc.

--
Attachment: cloudops_procurement_checklist.pdf (pdf stub)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Maria Torres <maria@cloudops.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer — pricing structure and channel routing question

Hi Maria — great to meet you yesterday.

Short answers up front:
- We can produce a multi-region private-offer pricing grid that shows list price, committed tiers, and the effective customer unit price after committed discounts. We typically show both AWS list price and a flattened effective price for procurement.
- For channel routing we support both: a dealer (distributor) pass-through and a reseller netback. The common pattern is to route a dealer fee (fixed % of net) to the distributor and set a separate reseller margin at the partner level. We can document exact invoice flows for NorthGate.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll attach a draft private-offer PDF and a pricing workbook with SKU rows and two margin columns (dealer pass-through %, reseller netback %).
2) Ben (cc’d) will confirm recommended baseline margins for a first-close deal and any accelerate/commit bands.
3) Can we book a 30-min call Tue 9/8 09:00 PT to walk procurement + NorthGate through routing flows? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Items I need from you before the call: approximate committed ARR by region (or a rough % split), and whether NorthGate will invoice on your behalf or if CloudOps expects Redwood to invoice and pass through credits.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Draft private offer + SKU-to-margin workbook (CO-2026-091)

Maria — attaching the materials for the call.

Attachments: pricing_workbook_v3.xlsx (xlsx stub), PrivateOffer_CO-2026-091.pdf (pdf stub)

What’s inside:
- PrivateOffer_CO-2026-091.pdf: draft AWS private-offer payload with list prices and proposed committed tiers. This is a working draft; legal/redlines expected.
- pricing_workbook_v3.xlsx: SKU-level rows with columns: SKU, UNIT_LIST, COMMIT_TIER_1, COMMIT_TIER_2, DEAL_EFFECTIVE_PRICE, DEALER_PASS_THROUGH_PCT, RESELLER_NETBACK_PCT. I pre-filled suggested margins: dealer pass-through 8% at baseline, reseller netback 10% (separate) — Ben, please update if you recommend different splits for NorthGate.

Two operational caveats to flag before the Tue call:
1) Geo price tilt: AWS marketplace enforces a single private-offer object per region; if you require list parity across regions we can set list prices to be within the 12% tolerance you mentioned but committed discounts can vary by region. If procurement requires identical effective pricing across regions we’ll need to compress commit tiers which can impact Redwood’s unit economics (we've modeled ~5-7% additional margin pressure).

2) Invoicing path: Redwood prefers to invoice the buyer directly and apply partner commission via a monthly settlement to the distributor (pass-through). If CloudOps requires distributor invoicing (NorthGate invoices CloudOps), we’ll need a short legal amendment to the PO flow and reseller agreement to accommodate tax/invoice routing.

Action items:
- Maria: confirm approximate regional ARR split and NorthGate invoicing preference before Tue.
- Ben: propose final margin split and any accelerate bands by EOD Mon.
- Laura: ops checklist — can you review the workbook and flag anything missing for marketplace publication?

DocSig/links: I pushed the private-offer draft to HubSpot (record CO-2026-091) and included a preview in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-pricing-playbook
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/89765

Best,

Subject: Re: Draft private offer + SKU-to-margin workbook (CO-2026-091)

Thanks Rishi — looked through the workbook this morning. A few quick notes before the Tue walk-through: 

- Dealer vs reseller split: for deals routed through distributors we typically recommend an 18% dealer pass-through at the distributor layer if NorthGate will provide value-add (billing/techsupport). That can be structured as an invoice settlement (dealer fee) rather than altering AWS list lines. If we keep dealer pass-through at 18%, then a 7-10% reseller netback is acceptable for downstream partners depending on attach services.

- Geo tilt: agree with Rishi — if CloudOps insists on effective-price parity across NA/EU/APAC we need to flatten commit discounts which will raise list price in lower-cost regions. Recommend we present two options on Tue: (A) list price parity with compressed commit discounts, (B) regional list tilt within 12% with region-specific commits.

- Attachments: I added a brief ops tab to the workbook for marketplace publication checklist (required SKUs, metering type, entitlements). Also included a short tax note re: distributor invoicing (sales_tax_handling.txt stub).

Ben — can you confirm the recommended margin bands and whether we want an early-adopter uplift (extra 2% dealer fee for 12-month commit)?

I’ll join the Tue call and ask Marketplace ops to be on standby in case they need to approve SKU entitlements.

Laura Bennett
Head of Deal Operations | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
